question: Should core recursively inspect opaque `channelData` keys and values and drop the entire payload when protected internal runtime context is detected?
rationale: This is a deliberate trust-boundary policy for provider-owned opaque data; tests can prove behavior, but only the owning maintainer can confirm that fail-closed deletion belongs in core and is preferable to owner-plugin sanitization.

options.title: Approve fail-closed core filtering
options.body: Keep the recursive check so protected context cannot leave through opaque channel payloads, accepting that mixed safe and unsafe payloads are wholly discarded.

options.title: Move filtering to payload owners
options.body: Require channel or provider implementations to sanitize their typed payloads, preserving core opacity but risking inconsistent protection across owners.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed core filtering
recommendation.body: Keep the recursive check so protected context cannot leave through opaque channel payloads, accepting that mixed safe and unsafe payloads are wholly discarded.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows direct involvement in landing and securing the message-tool boundary, making this the strongest available routing candidate for the policy choice.
